name: OpenLoop Pattern Finder
idea: Free, AI-free search engine for crochet and knit patterns that links out to designers' own sites and filters properly.
description: People are leaving 1-3 star reviews on pattern apps because almost everything sits behind a Pro paywall, the photos look AI-generated, and there is no real search or free-only filter. This is a PWA index of free, human-made patterns (title, thumbnail link, yarn weight, hook/needle size, skill level, item type, time) that always sends the visitor to the designer's own page so ads and affiliate links are preserved. Moat: a hand-curated, normalised pattern dataset (yarn-weight and gauge normalisation, dedup across sites) and designer-friendly link-out, which scraper apps are being blamed for ignoring.
web_delivery: Next.js/Vite PWA on Vercel hobby, Supabase Postgres full-text search for the index; no uploads or media hosting (thumbnails hot-linked or omitted).
why_hard_to_copy: The value is the curated, de-duplicated and normalised free-pattern index with designer opt-in; the code is easy but the dataset and designer trust take months of manual work.

name: TankLog Free
idea: Aquarium journal with unlimited free water-test logging, charts, dosing maths and a species list you can extend.
description: AquaticLog introduced a cap of about five to ten logged measurements a month on the free tier, and fish-keeping apps are criticised for small species catalogs, no way to add your own fish, and no incompatibility warnings. The web app logs unlimited parameters per tank, plots trends, calculates dose volumes and water-change maths, and lets users add custom species and check stocking compatibility. Moat: a curated species/compatibility table and correct chemistry calculators (tank volume net of substrate, product dosing, KH/GH/CO2 relationships).
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel with Supabase auth and tables for tanks, tests and species; charts rendered client-side; installable on a phone for bench-side logging.
why_hard_to_copy: The logger is simple, but the hand-curated compatibility/dosing data and correct calculators are not; building trust takes community seeding.

name: Gigbook
idea: Browser-based band songbook and setlist manager with ChordPro import, correct transposition and shared live setlists, without a forced subscription.
description: OnSong's 2026 version moved features behind a subscription, long-time one-time-purchase users say features were locked and old libraries cannot be searched or transposed without paying, and tab apps are criticised for monthly pricing. Gigbook is a PWA where a band shares one library and setlist, each member sees their own key or capo, and charts display full-screen on a tablet or phone. Moat: robust ChordPro/OnSong-format and plain-text chord sheet parsing, enharmonic-correct transposition (flats, sharps, Nashville numbers, slash chords) and shared real-time setlist state.
web_delivery: PWA with service worker for offline gigs; Supabase Realtime for shared setlists; chord sheets stored as text so no media hosting.
why_hard_to_copy: Chord-sheet parsing and transposition edge cases plus real-time shared setlist sync; incumbents (BandHelper, OnSong) have years of format compatibility.

name: PlainRSVP
idea: Invite and RSVP page for bigger parties that works for every guest without an Apple ID, with spreadsheet import and name-based non-responder tracking.
description: Apple Invites reviewers complain that guests are tracked by email address, that Android and non-iCloud guests cannot open or answer invitations, and that you cannot import a spreadsheet or a Contacts group when you invite dozens of people. PlainRSVP gives each host one public link plus per-guest links, bulk import from CSV or vCard, household and plus-one handling, meal or dietary questions, and a 'who has not answered' list shown by name with copy-paste nudge texts. Moat is thin: the value is in guest-list import/dedup logic and polish, not in anything a determined vibe coder could not build.
web_delivery: Vercel-hosted web app with Supabase tables for events, guests and responses; guests only open a link, no install or account; email reminders via Supabase/Resend free tier.
why_hard_to_copy: Honestly weak: Partiful already offers no-app RSVP. Only guest-list import and household/dedup logic, plus wedding-style extras (meal choice, seating), give a small edge.

name: BirdTrip
idea: Offline-first birding PWA: log checklists with no pack download, plan trips for any location, and export in eBird upload format.
description: eBird's official app is blocking many users at a mandatory 'install a pack' screen, restricts exploring and logging to roughly a 30-mile radius, and made adding photos harder; several reviewers say to just use the website. BirdTrip is a phone-friendly PWA that stores the species list locally, lets you pick any hotspot or region before a trip, tallies counts offline and exports a CSV in eBird's record format for upload. Moat: offline-first sync, taxonomy and hotspot data integration and export-format correctness.
web_delivery: Installable PWA with service worker, IndexedDB for offline checklists and Supabase for sync; location through the browser's one-shot geolocation (no background GPS).
why_hard_to_copy: Offline-first sync, taxonomy handling and eBird export-format correctness, plus integration with public eBird hotspot/frequency data; a vibe coder can make a tally counter but not the data layer.

name: PracticeLoop
idea: Free web practice planner for musicians that cycles an exercise through all 12 keys and ladders tempo, with an accurate browser metronome and a shareable routine for teachers.
description: Modacity users report that after a redesign the free tier limits practice items and lists and hides the history, and that you cannot create one item across many keys; users of Practice Space want to enter time without running a timer and see longer-term graphs. PracticeLoop lets you define an exercise once and run it through all keys or a circle-of-fourths order, raise tempo in steps automatically, log time manually or by timer, and share a routine link with a teacher. Moat is modest: Web Audio scheduling accuracy and key-cycling logic.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel with Web Audio API metronome and Supabase storage for routines and logs; no audio files stored.
why_hard_to_copy: Sample-accurate Web Audio metronome scheduling and key-cycle/tempo-ladder logic are fiddly; the logging itself is easy to copy, so the moat is the practice engine and teacher sharing.

name: SwapSession
idea: Scheduled language-exchange sessions in the browser with fair half-and-half timers, goal-based matching and no dating-style profiles.
description: Tandem and Speaky reviewers say the apps feel like dating apps full of fake profiles, that multi-language use was easier before, and some were banned with no explanation. SwapSession matches people by language pair, level and time zone, books a time, opens a peer-to-peer video room in the browser with a timer that splits the hour between the two languages, and keeps profiles light with no photo-first browsing. Moat is the matching and scheduling quality plus trust features, but a cold-start network problem is the real risk.
web_delivery: Next.js app on Vercel; Supabase auth, scheduling tables and Realtime for signalling; WebRTC peer-to-peer video so no media is hosted.
why_hard_to_copy: Time-zone and level matching with session scheduling, reputation and reporting; network effects in a language-pair niche. The cold start is hard for the builder too.

name: ChartWright
idea: Knitting and crochet chart editor in the browser whose written instructions are correct for flat versus in-the-round work.
description: A paying knitting-chart app user says the written instructions come out wrong when switching a chart from flat to in the round (rows read left to right while the knits and purls are not reversed); another says large colourwork charts such as corner-to-corner are painful because zooming and panning draw random cells. ChartWright is a canvas chart editor with a stitch-symbol grammar that converts charts to written lines and back, handles right-side/wrong-side reversal, repeats and stitch-count changes, and works with a stylus or mouse with proper pan/zoom. Moat is the domain logic.
web_delivery: Canvas/SVG editor as a PWA on Vercel; charts stored as JSON in Supabase; PNG/PDF export client-side.
why_hard_to_copy: Correctness-critical stitch grammar (RS/WS reversal, in-the-round, repeats, increases/decreases changing counts) plus a large-chart editor; knitters will spot errors immediately.

signals.summary: Review "Not for designers": written instructions do not follow right-side/wrong-side logic when switching from flat to in the round; they read left to right and the knits and purls are not reversed.
signals.engagement: 9 of 15 recent reviews are 1-3 stars; this is the clearest logic bug
